label: Chokepoints tighten
summary: Friday belongs to the chokepoints. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed a US unmanned vessel at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and UK maritime monitors logged projectiles striking two ships off Oman; a day earlier the Houthis took Mocha, tightening their hold on Bab al-Mandeb. Oil near $108 drove 30-year US Treasury yields to their highest since 2007 and lifted Fed rate-hike odds to about 70 percent. Algeria severed relations with the UAE. Brazil's Supreme Court cancelled a second day of sittings amid a banking scandal, and Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak still kills close to half those infected. Against that: Putin and Xi landed in Delhi for a BRICS summit, Taiwan's vice president appeared openly at an Italian democracy forum, New York marked 25 years since 9/11, and BepiColombo reached Mercury. The weighted formula gave 39; no editorial adjustment.
